title: Trump's February 25 Memorandum Targets Covington & Burling
description_short: Trump's February 25, 2025 memorandum directed clearance suspensions for specified Covington lawyers and federal reviews of the firm's engagements and contracts.
description_medium: On February 25, 2025, Donald Trump signed a presidential memorandum directing agencies to suspend specified Covington & Burling security clearances pending review, terminate federal engagements where permitted by law, and have OMB review the firm's contracts. The source identifies a memorandum, not a March 14 executive order. The documents establish directives, not their eventual implementation or outcome.
description_long: On February 25, 2025, Donald Trump signed a presidential memorandum titled “Suspension of Security Clearances and Evaluation of Government Contracts.” It directed executive departments and agencies to take lawful steps to suspend active clearances held by Peter Koski and Covington & Burling members, partners, and employees who assisted former Special Counsel Jack Smith, pending a review of their roles and responsibilities. The memo also directed agencies to take steps to terminate Covington engagements to the maximum extent permitted by law and consistent with a separate Office of Management and Budget memorandum. It instructed OMB to issue a memorandum directing all agencies to review government contracts with the firm. The White House described the action as a memorandum and stated its rationale in terms of “weaponization of the judicial process”; that is the administration’s stated justification, not an independently established finding about the lawyers. The official documents verify issuance and the directions. They do not show whether clearances were ultimately suspended, contracts ended, or engagements terminated. The stored March 14, 2025 date and “executive order” label are incorrect for this action. This record covers the February 25 memorandum and its stated directives only.

source_fact_map.fact: The action was a February 25, 2025 presidential memorandum.
source_fact_map.source_excerpt:
February 25, 2025

MEMORANDUM FOR THE SECRETARY OF STATE THE SECRETARY OF DEFENSE THE ATTORNEY GENERAL THE SECRETARY OF ENERGY THE DIRECTOR OF THE OFFICE OF MANAGEMENT AND BUDGET THE DIRECTOR OF NATIONAL INTELLIGENCE THE DIRECTOR OF THE CENTRAL INTELLIGENCE AGENCY THE DIRECTOR OF THE OFFICE OF PERSONNEL MANAGEMENT

SUBJECT: Suspension of Security Clearances and Evaluation of Government Contracts I hereby direct the Attorney General and all other relevant heads of executive departments and agencies (agencies) to immediately take steps consistent with applicable law to suspend any active security clearances held by Peter Koski and all members, partners, and employees of Covington & Burling LLP who assisted former Special Counsel Jack Smith during his time as Special Counsel, pending a review and determination of their roles and responsibilities, if any, in the weaponization of the judicial process. I also direct the Attorney General and heads of agencies to take such actions as are necessary to terminate any engagement of Covington & Burling LLP by any agency to the maximum extent permitted by law and consistent with the memorandum that shall be issued by the Director of the Office of Management and Budget. Additionally, if any of the covered Covington & Burling LLP members, partners, and employees referenced in this memorandum obtained a security clearance from an agency not included as an addressee of this memorandum, the Director of the Office of Personnel Management shall provide this memorandum to the appropriate clearance-granting agency to ensure compliance. I further direct the Director of the Office of Management and Budget to issue a memorandum to all agencies to review all Government contracts with Covington & Burling LLP.

title: Unverified Claim That Kash Patel Created FBI Media Investigation Unit
description_short: Internal draft of the unverified claim that Patel created an FBI unit targeting journalists; the accessed Reuters report concerns prior remarks, not a unit.
description_medium: The supplied entry alleges that Kash Patel created an FBI unit to investigate journalists and media organizations critical of Trump. A Reuters report on his January 2025 confirmation hearing discusses questions about past remarks threatening investigations of news media; it does not identify or verify a unit. The allegation remains unverified and is not eligible for publication.
description_long: The supplied entry alleges that FBI Director Kash Patel created a dedicated unit inside the bureau to investigate journalists and media organizations that reported critically on Donald Trump. It further alleges that the unit was intended to suppress press freedom and intimidate newsrooms, and says attorneys and press-freedom organizations described it as an unprecedented threat. These statements remain allegations drawn from the frozen record; the packet does not identify the unit, a creation order, a launch date, a roster, or a journalist or organization investigated by it. A January 30, 2025 Reuters report says Democrats questioned Patel at his confirmation hearing about past comments threatening investigations of government officials and the news media. That report concerns his prior rhetoric and does not document a dedicated investigative unit. The accessible sources do not establish that this unit existed or operated on the frozen date of March 15, 2025. This internal draft preserves the supplied allegation while marking its core event unverified; it is not publication-ready.

The supplied AP URL is about Alien Enemies Act deportation flights, not family separation. The accessible April Guardian report documents renewed family detention, including families held at Karnes and Dilley, but does not establish that the government separated those parents and children from one another or formally reinstated zero tolerance. The later August 2025 reporting found in search concerns a different, later tactic and cannot repair the April date. No same-event narrower claim or quantity is supportable from this packet.
